delta: 'The arc of the descent: Vance stops trying to buy the vault with paper and starts paying for it
  with her brother. She begins at the slot board, certified and unslotted, believing that the obstacle
  is the co-op''s signature and that a signature can be argued for. Quiej refuses her, correctly and on
  the record, because the sealing order is posted and the co-op will not slot a descent that outlives
  its own indemnity. The refusal is logged, and the logging starts a clock nobody in the gallery can stop.
  What that clock is made of the reader learns from Ilan. One hundred and eighty hours before the refusal
  he went down on a co-op indemnity dive, on a cold soak cut to four hours, on the hard line because the
  rig loop his lungs were never certified to take. He found the read-key seating two fingers off the co-op''s
  drawing, seated it, and lost his left hand to the throat on the way back, because the throat runs on
  the co-op''s cycle and releases only from the vault side. He signed the indemnity on the deck of the
  lock with the hand he had left, and the co-op took the seating procedure out of him entire, which is
  lawful, and which is why nobody alive can say aloud what belongs in that slot. Vance goes down unslotted,
  finds the seating, finds it empty, and comes up with a shape and no name for it. That is where the paper
  runs out. In the second half she asks her brother, not for a memory the co-op owns but for what his
  hands still do, and his hands answer; what he gets back for it is the knowledge that something was taken.
  The steward holds her order to schedule while the shelf moves the window forward, and understands, too
  late to say so, that an order can stand on the board and fail in the water. By the close the core has
  been reached and the ring is known, and the cost of knowing it is on no co-op form: the truth between
  the Vances is spoken, the debt for the hand is answered, and what Vance wanted she has bought out of
  her brother rather than out of the co-op.'
